title: Tooltip
wrapsNative: help(_:), which sets the accessibility hint; accessibilityLabel(_:) for the name of the control
summary: iOS shows no tooltip. The help modifier carries the same supplementary text: on iOS and iPadOS it becomes the accessibility hint, and where the system has tooltips (an app running on a Mac, visionOS) it is shown as one. Monarch ships nothing, and nothing essential may live in help text.
whenToUse: To clarify what an icon-only control does, together with accessibilityLabel for its name. VoiceOver reads the name, then the help text as the hint.
whenNotToUse: Not for anything a person needs in order to use the screen: on a phone or tablet it is never seen. Put that text on screen, or in a popover opened by an info button.
api: func help(_ text: String) -> some View
func accessibilityLabel(_ label: String) -> some View
func accessibilityHint(_ hint: String) -> some View

states.name: VoiceOver
states.description: The help text is read as the hint, after the name and a pause.

states.name: pointer on a Mac or visionOS
states.description: The system shows the help text beside the control after a short delay.

appearance: Nothing is drawn on iOS and iPadOS. Where the system shows a tooltip it draws it itself; Monarch colours and type are not applied.
platformNotes: The web Tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus, with a side, an alignment and a delay. The parity map expected help(_:) to show on pointer and keyboard on iPad; according to the SwiftUI documentation it shows a help tag only on macOS and visionOS and otherwise configures the accessibility hint, so on iPadOS a pointer shows nothing. The web's content must become plain text. Android uses the Material 3 PlainTooltip, which opens on long press; iOS has no equivalent, so a control that needs explaining on touch gets a visible label, or an info button that opens a popover.
accessibility: An icon-only control needs accessibilityLabel for its name; help is not a name.
help(_:) configures the accessibility hint, so VoiceOver reads it after the name. accessibilityHint(_:) sets the hint directly when the spoken text should differ.
Write the hint as the result of the action ("Shows only unpaid invoices"), without the word button and without the name again.
People can turn hints off in VoiceOver settings, so a hint must not carry information the label lacks.
edgeCases: On an iPhone and an iPad the help text is never visible.
Keep the text to one short sentence; it is read aloud in full.
The reason a control is disabled belongs on screen, not in help text.
